newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche sees no court case over Horlick.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche sees no court case over Horlick.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG does not expect to go to court with Nicola Horlick, the fund manager who resigned from its London-based funds unit but alleges constructive dismissal, a senior Deutsche official said.

Deutsche board member Rolf Breuer, who is poised to take over from Hilmar Kopper at the helm of Deutsche in May, said "The facts are clear. Mrs Horlick inflicted damage on the bank with her attempt to poach staff and then resigned."
Breuer was speaking at a bourse event in Frankfurt on Monday evening.

Horlick, once Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's top pension fund manager, resigned her position last Thursday amid a blaze of publicity, having been suspended after allegations that she tried to lure a team of colleagues to another bank.

The 35-year-old's lawyer said on Monday that Horlick, who denies the charges and says she wants compensation or reinstatement, would consider legal action if she failed to reach an amicable settlement with her former employers.
She travelled on Friday to Deutsche Bank's Frankfurt headquarters, insisting she wanted to speak to a board member at the bank.

Horlick met a senior legal officer of the bank and a top personnel executive, and has expressed interest in pursuing those talks, Deutsche was quick to stress that London would be the venue for future talks.
